title: GOD'S SOVEREIGN HAND OVER THE NATIONS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So we went on past our relatives the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. We turned from the Arabah road, which comes up from Elath and Ezion Geber, and traveled along the desert road of Moab. Then the Lord said to me, "Do not harass the Moabites or provoke them to war, for I will not give you any part of their land. I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as a possession." - Deut 2:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Again God tells Israel to pass by peaceably — this time the Moabites, descendants of Lot, Abraham's nephew. Their land, too, was not for Israel to take, because God had given it to them. Just as with Edom, God had appointed a territory for Moab, and Israel was to honour it. God was directing not only Israel's journey but the destinies of Moab, Edom, and Ammon as well.

What emerges clearly in this chapter is the sweeping sovereignty of God over all nations. He is not a local deity concerned only with one people. He gives lands, sets boundaries, and orders the histories of peoples across the earth. Edom, Moab, Ammon — each had received their portion from His hand. The God of Israel is the God of all the earth.

This is a truth that puts our world in perspective. Nations rise and fall, borders shift, empires come and go — and behind it all is a sovereign God who rules over the affairs of humanity. He is not distant or uninvolved. As Scripture says, He determines the times set for the nations and the boundaries of their lands (Acts 17:26). Nothing in history escapes His governance.

For us, this brings deep peace. In a world that often feels chaotic and out of control, our God reigns over it all. The same God who ordered the movements of ancient peoples is at work in our time, accomplishing His purposes. And His grand purpose across all history is the redemption He has brought in Christ, gathering people from every nation into His kingdom (Rev 7:9). We can rest, knowing that the sovereign Lord of the nations is our faithful Father, working all things toward His good and glorious end.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does God's sovereignty over the nations bring you peace in a chaotic world?
2. Do you trust that God is at work in the affairs of your time?
3. How does God's plan to gather all nations in Christ shape your hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign Lord, You rule over all nations and order all of history. In a world that feels chaotic, help me rest in Your reign, trusting that You are working all things toward Your glorious purpose in Christ. Amen.
